summary: MistServer is a public domain streaming media server written in C++. It is designed to ingest and deliver media content across various devices and formats. The software provides a backend infrastructure for distributing video and audio streams.
goodFor: This is a suitable option if you need an unrestrictive public domain license for a custom media distribution pipeline. It fits technical setups requiring direct handling of streaming formats.
watchOut: The repository has a moderate developer following and community size, which may limit the availability of troubleshooting resources. You should expect to rely heavily on self-support for complex integration issues.
deployNotes: As a C++ application, you will typically need to run it behind a reverse proxy to handle TLS termination. You should also ensure adequate persistent storage is available if you plan to store media files locally.
